query: For a high-entropy alloy designed as a single-phase solid solution and exhibiting a favorable strength–ductility combination, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to preserve toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading? Explain the hypothesized mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the same alloy tested under identical conditions without the intervention, define the applicable exposure and loading regime, identify supporting evidence from prior observations, and specify an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of a controlled amount of grain boundary segregants will preserve toughness in a high-entropy alloy after thermal exposure and subsequent loading.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase solid solution high-entropy alloy with favorable strength–ductility combination
generation.intervention: Introduction of controlled amount of grain boundary segregants
generation.conditions: Thermal exposure at 800°C for 10 hours followed by uniaxial tensile loading at room temperature
generation.mechanism: The grain boundary segregants will inhibit grain boundary embrittlement and promote grain boundary sliding, thereby preserving toughness
generation.predicted_outcome: The alloy with grain boundary segregants will exhibit higher toughness compared to the same alloy without segregants under identical conditions
generation.baseline: Toughness of the alloy without grain boundary segregants
generation.boundary: Thermal exposure temperature and duration, loading rate and magnitude
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount and type of grain boundary segregants, the effect of segregants on strength

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the toughness of the alloy with and without grain boundary segregants after thermal exposure and loading
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloy with grain boundary segregants exhibits lower or equal toughness compared to the alloy without segregants, the hypothesis is falsified
